title: Rhythm & Micro-Timing Skill
purpose: Make the melody sound human by understanding rubato, groove, and phrasing — NOT robotic grid-quantization.
core_principles: Humans do not sing exactly on the grid. Every real performance has tiny delays and hurries (micro-timing).
A melody with perfect grid timing sounds mechanical and lifeless.
The expressive identity of a song lives in its micro-timing, phrasing and dynamic shape — preserve these.

rubato.definition: Slight, tasteful deviations in tempo for expressive effect — holding a note a touch longer or pushing forward through a phrase.
rubato.action: Keep the RAW onset times from the pitch/onset analysis. Do NOT aggressively re-quantize to a strict grid. A 20-50ms offset from the beat is musical, not an error.

phrasing.definition: Grouping notes into musical sentences, with a natural breath (short rest) between phrases.
phrasing.action: Notes within a phrase connect smoothly (legato). A real gap between phrases = a breath/rest. Preserve these gaps.
phrasing.dynamic_shape: Phrases usually swell slightly toward their peak then relax — shape velocities accordingly (crescendo into the climax, decrescendo out).

groove.definition: The rhythmic feel created by consistent, subtle timing accents (e.g. slightly swinging the eighths).
groove.note: Detect the consistent offset pattern from the beat and preserve it for a natural groove.

legato_vs_staccato.legato: Connected, overlapping notes (smooth). Use when notes are close in time with no breath.
legato_vs_staccato.staccato: Short, detached notes. Use for light, punctuated passages.
legato_vs_staccato.action: Detect the gap between consecutive notes: small gap -> legato (overlap); large gap -> rest.
